question: Record temperatures in recent months have resulted in mass fish deaths from suffocation in Orbetello lagoon. The fisheries sector has been brought to its knees and the tourist season has been severely affected – a situation that has been reoccurring for a number of years. The lagoon has been named an SCI and SPA1, and is classified as a wetland of national interest under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.

On 1 August 2024, the President of the Region of Tuscany declared a natural disaster and provided funding of EUR 1 million: EUR 350 000 million to dispose of the dead fish carcasses, and an additional EUR 650 000 to support local fishers and the tourist and commercial activities affected.

The Law on the management of Orbetello lagoon, which would allow for the introduction and implementation of structural interventions to protect the ecosystem, has been blocked at national level, leading to unacceptable delays. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this ongoing situation in the lagoon?
Has the Italian Government made any specific demands to the European Commission? If so, under which fund has it requested aid from the Commission?
Site of Community Importance and Special Area of Conservation.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.11.2024) 1. The Commission had contact on the situation in the Orbetello lagoon and the resulting damages with the Managing Authority of the European Regional Development Fund1 Regional Programme (ERDF RP) for Tuscany to explore potential interventions. 2. The Commission has not received any request from the Italian government concerning this situation.

In the framework of the ERDF RP for Tuscany 2021-2027, there are no interventions planned to repair damages to the fishing sector and tourism. The ERDF RP for Tuscany is focused on risk prevention, including on the construction of infrastructures to prevent natural risks (hydraulic, hydrogeological and drought).

Competent authorities can consider mobilising financing from the European Maritime Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF)2 allocated to the Italian Programme to provide support to the fisheries sector, while enhancing its capacity to manage and respond to such risks in the future.

The activation of EMFAF financial support should be in line with the objectives of the Italian EMFAF Programme as agreed between the Commission and Italy. The affected parties should coordinate with the relevant Italian authorities to apply for such support.
